1.title: Yum, a Bun!
1.topic: baking buns at home with Mom (family, food, cooking)
lines: *Mom* and I | *mix* and *mix*.
*Pat* it, | *pat* it, | *pat* it *flat*.
Put the *buns* | in the *pan*.
In they *go*. | *Wait*, | *wait*, | *wait*.
*Ding*! | The buns are *hot*! ↘
*Yum*, | *yum*! | I *love* a *bun*! ↘
sounds: 입을 옆으로 크게 벌리고 '애'에 가깝게 짧게 말해요.
bun, yum의 u는 힘을 빼고 짧게 '어'. '분'이 아니라 '번'이에요.
느낌표 문장은 크고 신나게, 끝은 내려요.
1.expression: Stir a big bowl on “mix and mix,” pat your hand on “pat it flat,” whisper the three “wait”s, jump on “Ding!”, and rub your tummy on “Yum, yum!”

2.title: Rainy Day Recess
2.topic: rain keeps the class inside at recess and the teacher brings out games (school, weather, feelings)
lines: On Monday, | it *rained* | and *rained*.
“No recess *outside* today,” | said Ms. *Bell*. ↘
Tom *frowned*. | “But I *wanted* to play *tag*!”
Then Ms. Bell *pulled* out | a big *box* of *games*.
The class *played* freeze *dance* | and *hopped* like *frogs*.
Tom *jumped* so *high* | that everyone *giggled*.
“Can we do this *tomorrow*?” ↗ | asked Tom.
Ms. Bell *laughed*. | “Only if it *rains*!” ↘
vocab: 음악이 멈추면 얼음! 하는 춤 놀이
sounds: n, l, y 뒤의 -ed는 짧은 d 소리: rained '레인드'.
p, f 소리 뒤의 -ed는 t 소리: hopped '합트'. '합페드'가 아니에요.
t 뒤의 -ed는 '이드'로 한 박자 더: want-ed '원티드'.
2.expression: Sound gloomy on the rain and Tom's frown, get bouncy and excited for the games, ask “Can we do this tomorrow?” with hope, and give Ms. Bell's last line a playful laugh.

3.title: A Visit to the Fire Station
3.topic: a class field trip to the fire station and the safety rule for a smoke alarm (community, school, safety)
lines: Last Friday, | our class took a *trip* | to the *fire* station | on Oak Street.
A firefighter named *Captain* Rosa | met us at the big red *door*.
First, | she showed us the *fire* truck. | It was *shiny* and *enormous*!
We saw the long *ladder* | and the *hoses* | rolled up on the side.
Then Captain Rosa put on her *gear*: | a *heavy* coat, | boots, | a *helmet*, | and a *mask*.
She looked a little *scary*, | but she *smiled* and said, | “It's still *me*!”
She told us what to do | if we ever hear a *smoke* alarm.
“Get *low*, | get *out*, | and *stay* out!” ↘
At the end, | we each got a *sticker* | and sat in the *driver's* seat.
Now I know | firefighters are *helpers*, | even when they wear their *masks*. ↘
sounds: 긴 단어는 힘주는 음절 하나만 크고 길게, 나머지는 약하게.
두 단어가 합쳐진 이름은 앞 단어에 힘을 줘요.
a heavy coat, boots, a helmet, and a mask
목록은 쉼표마다 살짝 올리다가 마지막 'and a mask'에서 내려요.
3.expression: Tell it like an excited reporter back from a field trip: amazed at the truck, a little nervous at the mask, then loud and clear on the safety rule “Get low, get out, and stay out!”

4.title: Bram Builds a Dam
4.topic: a proud young beaver tries to build a dam alone before winter and learns to accept help (animals, seasons, teamwork, feelings)
lines: At the edge of a quiet *forest*, | there lived a young beaver | named *Bram*.
Bram was *proud* of his strong *teeth* | and his flat, *paddle*-shaped tail.
One chilly *November* morning, | he decided to build | the *biggest* dam | the river had ever *seen*.
“I don't need *anyone's* help,” | he *announced*. | “I can do it *all* by *myself*.” ↘
Day after day, | Bram *chewed* through branches | and *dragged* them into the *stream*.
But every *night*, | the rushing water | *pulled* his sticks *apart*.
A *muskrat* paddled over | and *offered* to bring some *mud*.
“*No*, thank you,” | Bram said *stiffly*. | “This is *my* dam.”
Soon the *first* snowflakes began to *fall*, | and Bram's paws were *sore* and *tired*.
He sat on the riverbank | and stared at the *pile* | of *loose* sticks.
“Maybe | I can't do it *alone*,” | he *whispered*. ↘
The next morning, | Bram *asked* the muskrat, | the *otters*, | and two *ducks* for help.
The ducks *gathered* reeds, | the otters *rolled* stones, | and the muskrat *packed* the mud.
By *sunset*, | the dam stood *strong* | against the *icy* water.
All winter long, | the pond stayed *calm* and *deep*, | and Bram never *forgot* | what his friends had *taught* him:
*Many* paws | make *light* work. ↘
sounds: “I don't need anyone's help.” / “Maybe I can't do it alone.”
처음엔 크고 자신만만하게, 나중엔 작고 조용하게 — 브램의 마음이 바뀐 걸 목소리로 보여 줘요.
교훈 문장은 천천히, 끊어서, 끝을 확실히 내려요.
4.expression: Read it like a storyteller: proud and bossy for Bram at first, worried as the snow falls, soft and honest on “Maybe I can't do it alone,” busy and cheerful as the friends work, and slow and wise on the moral.
